quest.title: When All Becomes a Monument
quest.description: Side by side with Mavuika, you defeat Gosoythoth and emerge as a hero revered by all in Natlan. Take this moment to enjoy the glory that is rightfully yours.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Primogem x30, Mora x53900, The Cornerstone of Stars and Flames x1, Pilgrim's Chronicle x1, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Your friends cheer for your return as the people of Natlan celebrate your victory.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: In the interest of safety, you allow a doctor to check for signs of Abyssal corrosion.

dialogues.speaker: Louqua
dialogues.text: Unbelievable... No signs of Abyssal corruption whatsoever. The same goes for the Pyro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Louqua
dialogues.text: In that case, just get some rest, and enjoy your victory.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That means... There's officially nothing to worry about!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You won, hahahaha! You actually won!

choices.text: Finally, it's time to relax.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knew you could do it! The Abyss is no match for you!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: #You did it again, {NICKNAME}. Your strength is remarkable!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: And now, Natlan is finally free from the threat of the Abyss!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Welcome back, great hero... I can't wait to tell your story to everyone!

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: We should record it on a woven scroll, too. That way, your story will be preserved in my tribe for generations to come.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: I'm sure the Grannies and Gramps back home are already on it.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: #Amazing job, {NICKNAME}. Becoming the first outlander with an ancient name definitely makes you a legend.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The Lord of the Night was right to place her trust in you. She chose the perfect name.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Th—The most important thing is that you made it back safe! Now, I don't have to worry about the rescue plan!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You came up with a rescue plan?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: #W—Well, {NICKNAME} already saved me once. So, yeah... If things got risky down there, I was gonna charge in and rescue {M#him}{F#her}!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: I don't think it would be quite so simple, Kachina. But, still...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: If something like that really did happen, I'd come for you, too, no matter what it took.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Couldn't have said it better myself!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Bravery aside, I try not to act on impulse... But, I suppose there's an exception to every rule.

choices.text: Before you praise me too much...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: In the Ley Lines, I encountered many souls of the dead, and I could hear everyone rooting for me from above.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, really? Who did you see?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I saw Atea, Vichama, Chuychu, and all six heroes from five hundred years ago... Not to mention, I heard the messages you left for me in my ancient name.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have to thank each and every one of you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Without your help, I could never have defeated an enemy as strong as the Abyss.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: So, you heard everything we said...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Those messages became part of your name during the forging process. I just didn't expect them to come in handy at such a crucial moment...

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: To think that you heard them, though... Th—That's a little embarrassing...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hey, what's embarrassing about that? I'll say it again right now!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Being your friend makes me so happy! Hehehe~

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Heh, good one, Chuychu.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: #Things are looking lively over here. How are you feeling, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I feel completely fine.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Great, just what I wanted to hear.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The preparations for your celebration ceremony are almost complete.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Celebration ceremony?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: According to tradition, we hold a celebration ceremony for our most outstanding warriors after their final Pilgrimage.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: In most cases, "outstanding" means warriors who earned more than twenty victories in the Night Warden Wars.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: It's an exceedingly rare honor. You can think of it almost like a lifetime achievement award.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: We haven't held one of those ceremonies in a long time, though...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: #True, but given {NICKNAME}'s exceptional contribution to this victory, I think {M#he}{F#she} is more than worthy of the honor.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Let's head to the center of the Stadium, and I'll announce the honor to everyone. You deserve a formal round of applause for this achievement.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Oooh, then I'm gonna grab the best seat in the house!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Wait, I—I'm coming, too!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: Kamera... This calls for a Kamera...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha, slow down! There's no rush!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mavuika, if this ceremony is to celebrate defeating the Abyss, don't you deserve the same honor?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: What's the point of holding a victory feast for yourself? Besides, I'm already the Pyro Archon — that's enough honor for a lifetime.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Let's go. Everyone's waiting for us.

choices.text: I have something to say.
Finally, someone to speak for me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that all Paimon is to you...? You know what? Never mind. You get a free pass on all Paimon-teasing today!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Today, Natlan's long struggle against the Abyss has met its end.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Many fought for this day and gave their lives for this cause — we must not forget them, or the heroic outlander who lent us their aid.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #{M#His}{F#Her} ancient name, "Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini," will be immortalized in the history of Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: From this point on, there will be no more Night Warden Wars, and I pray the Ode of Resurrection will never again need to bring back the fallen.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We fought for a singular purpose — peace. And now, it has been achieved.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #The funeral to commemorate the fallen will be held on a later day. In the meantime, our hero will embark on a parade of blessings. Let us send h{M#im}{F#er} off with a round of applause.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #And show h{M#im}{F#er} the warmth and gratitude of our people!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Wohoooooo!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Go on, this is your moment. You should savor it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But... what about you?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Now that the threat of the Abyss has been eliminated, we finally have a chance to restore the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'll take care of that first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! We'll look forward to good news!

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Just a moment, great hero. Before you set out on the parade of blessings, please accept these feathered accessories.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: We bestow these gifts to every hero who receives this honor. They are proof of your bravery and strength and mark you as a role model for all in Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Thank you for everything... Thank you for saving us from the Abyss!

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Now, the person who has the honor of adorning you with these gifts is none other than one of Natlan's most outstanding warriors, Chasca!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's just someone we know.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You sound disappointed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: By "someone we know," Paimon meant "a cherished comrade."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly! It, uh... makes this moment even more special because we're already friends!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Well... Both in a personal capacity and as a representative of all warriors in Natlan, I bestow upon you this blessing.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: May your flame forever burn pure and bright.

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: With us by your side, you'll never fight alone!

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Time to embark on your parade of blessings.

dialogues.speaker: Balam
dialogues.text: Great hero... Could I have a moment of your time?

dialogues.speaker: Balam
dialogues.text: A lot of people here really look up to you and would love get a picture or an autograph.

dialogues.speaker: Balam
dialogues.text: You don't mind indulging them for a little bit, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, look at all the people... They must have been waiting here for a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #That doesn't sound like too much to ask, right {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Alright.

response.speaker: Balam
response.text: That's right! The photo booth is this way, and the autograph area is over there.

response.speaker: Balam
response.text: The parade of blessings will continue in that direction. So, head to the next area whenever you're ready — we'll be cheering for you!

choices.text: Just a few photos and autographs, right?

dialogues.speaker: Wakanka
dialogues.text: Yes, that's it!

dialogues.speaker: Nusta
dialogues.text: Thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Wakanka
dialogues.text: That pose is perfect!

dialogues.speaker: Waniyetu
dialogues.text: Such a precious memento...

dialogues.speaker: Wakanka
dialogues.text: Wow, it looks great!

dialogues.speaker: Aucaman
dialogues.text: Can I have one more photo? Just one more!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry, only one photo per person! There's still a lot of people waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Aucaman
dialogues.text: It's okay — one is enough! One is more than enough!

dialogues.speaker: Wakanka
dialogues.text: Look over here... Perfect! This is going straight into the next issue.

dialogues.speaker: Yaretzi
dialogues.text: Thank you, hero... Thank you so much for everything you've done for Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Wakanka
dialogues.text: Alright, that's all the film. No more pictures, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Eluney
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Wakanka
dialogues.text: We can't keep our great hero here forever. Thank you for your participation and your understanding, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, everyone's so enthusiastic... Paimon bets she could make a small fortune by selling photos of you to people in Natlan!

choices.text: Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, alright! It was just a joke!

choices.text: Don't even think about it.

dialogues.speaker: Wuttunee
dialogues.text: Line up, everyone. Single file, please! The hero will begin signing autographs.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What name should I sign...?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ("Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini"... seems like the obvious choice.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I'm starting to get the hang of this. Let's go for a few more...)

dialogues.speaker: Wampuna
dialogues.text: Sorry to bother you, great hero.

dialogues.speaker: Wampuna
dialogues.text: I'm a messenger from the Scions of the Canopy. I know everyone's been curious about the hidden message behind "Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini."

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: Every ancient name has a story behind it and comes with a certain mantra...

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: Usually, the Wayob reveal those mantras to our chiefs in a dream, but yours is still unknown to us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean like the lines the six heroes recited when they appeared!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #But, um, where do they come from? Is it something you have to decide, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In the beginning, there was darkness.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Until someone set themselves aflame.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Only then did the universe know light.

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Ohhhhhh...!

dialogues.speaker: Wampuna
dialogues.text: That was beautiful! I've got it all down!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the final element of your ancient name, right? That means you've been completely accepted by Natlan's Ley Lines!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Lord of the Night gave those words to me.

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: From the Lord of the Night herself...

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: Legendary! Truly legendary!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: "Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini! Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini! Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini!"

dialogues.speaker: Balam
dialogues.text: #We now arrive at the end of the parade of blessings. Let us offer {NICKNAME} our blessings one more time and give {M#him}{F#her} a resounding round of applause!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: WOOOHOOO!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #That's a hero's welcome if Paimon ever saw one, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You deserve it, of course! Considering the risk you took.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon! Finally! I was looking everywhere for you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali! Why didn't you come to the parade?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Never mind that! I have something important to tell you. Come with me!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I went to revisit the revelations in my dreams as soon as you came back from battle.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, I couldn't fall asleep just anywhere — I needed somewhere private. I didn't want anyone to overhear me sleep-talk or watch me contort myself into some weird position...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, that's not the important part! It's about Mavuika's death — her fate hasn't changed at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But, we both made it back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Didn't you defeat the bad guy behind all this? Does that mean the war isn't over?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No, the disaster is over, but my dreams never lie...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's why I came to find you. I need to know what I'm missing.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Where is Mavuika right now? Did she tell you what she's planning?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She said she was going to restore the Night Kingdom... Compared to fighting the Abyss, that should be pretty easy, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: After all, the corrosion should be gone by now...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Easy... not so much. We can't restore the Ley Lines without the Lord of the Night, and I'm not sure she has enough power to do it on her own.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The Lord of the Night is weak right now. She told us that herself, remember? I'll admit — restoring the Ley Lines is simpler than reconstructing them entirely, but it's still no easy feat...

choices.text: You've got a point...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True... If the Lord of the Night could restore the Ley Lines by herself, all Mavuika would need to do is tell her we won.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Not even that. The Lord of the Night knows the Ley Lines better than anyone. I'm sure she knew of your victory before us all.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Point being, this matter is far more complicated than the Archon made it out to be. We need to get to the bottom of this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But, why would she hide the truth from us?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Mavuika has accepted her death, remember? For her to let someone else dictate her end, there can be only one possibility...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: She must think the outcome of her death... is worth it.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The moment Mavuika used the Ruler of Death's power, death was demanded in return — not necessarily as repayment for her aid, but as a "rule."

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: That means Mavuika doesn't have to just sacrifice herself to the Ruler of Death. She can still use her death to get something in return.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Like... dying for a cause?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then, let's get going! Where do you think she went? Could it be where we found the Source Mechanism?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The Lord of the Night should now be able to appear anywhere in Natlan. What we need to know is where the Ruler of Death can be summoned.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: According to the Lord of the Night, the Ruler of Death is one of the shining Shades, an extremely elusive figure. Even woven scrolls dating back thousands of years have nearly no mentions of her.

choices.text: Mavuika once met Xbalanque.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! Xbalanque created the rules of Natlan by borrowing power from the Ruler of Death — that means he's met her before!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do you know where can find him? Or, um... his resting place?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Legend remembers him as a wise ruler, one who left little behind.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: But, there is a place we could check — Ochkanatlan, the ruins we now refer to as "Cinder City."

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It was built on the site of a Dragon city and became known as the first city of the Pyro Archon. That's mostly likely where Xbalanque met the Ruler of Death.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, then to Och... ka... Cinder City it is! Yeah, Paimon's gonna stick with that name.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's not easy to get there, so follow me — I'll take you.

choices.text: She told us about it before.
Otherwise, Mavuika wouldn't need to get involved.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: I have grown weary of the endless wait. The fate of this land is of no interest to me anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: However, you humans managed to meet the expectations of the Heavenly Principles... For that result, you deserve praise.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: Mavuika, as the price for using my power, I shall now bear witness to your death.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: And with you, the war that your nation has waged for more than a thousand years shall meet its end.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Mavuika!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Ah, you got here sooner than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wh—What are you doing!?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Closing the final chapter on the plan that has consumed Natlan for five hundred... no, for the entirety of our history.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We've eradicated the Abyss from Natlan, but its power remains in worlds beyond Teyvat, tremendous and unyielding.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Only by completely restoring the Night Kingdom can we defend against its corrosion in the long run.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But, the architect of the Night Kingdom is near her end. She lacks the power for such a task.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Worse still, if her life force is depleted, the rules of Natlan disappear along with her.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We have no need for the Ode of Resurrection right now, but it remains Natlan's strongest defense should the Abyss return one day.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So, you're planning to...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yes, my plan is to once again place my life within the Sacred Flame.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Five hundred years ago, I gave my life for the chance to be reborn in this era.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: A chance to see all my plans to completion. And now, to sustain the Lord of the Night, I will give my life once more.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: I respect your decision, Mavuika, but this method requires an immense sacrifice.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: The flames of your life force are exceedingly strong, but a life sustained by fire is one destined to die out one day. What will you do then?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I've thought about that... With the Abyss out of the picture for now, the Sacred Flame's power will be consumed at a much slower rate. My life force should be able to sustain it for another two or three hundred years.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Future Pyro Archons will continue to seek new sources of fire. As long as Natlan's legacy endures, the Night Kingdom will survive, impervious to the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: Once again, you place hope in the hands of the future...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, the Pilgrimage can replenish the power of the Sacred Flame! We can give it that meaning! Why shoulder this burden by yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Because, I want the Pilgrimage to change.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The Pilgrimage was an essential part of our struggle against the Abyss — a grand competition full of promise and glory. But, it also chained our people to an inescapable destiny.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Fear and anxiety have been our constant companions. We knew what the consequences would be if we laid down our arms. Morality left us with no other choice.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: And so, Natlan became the nation of war.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: This is where Xbalanque defeated the dragons and granted our people the liberation of their flesh. And now, in the same place, I have the chance to grant them the liberation of their spirit.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: There will be no war, only competition — one fueled by our dreams for the future rather than a desperate struggle for survival.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: A new future deserves a new meaning, a chance to take a definitive step forward.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Very noble indeed, but what does any of this have to do with you? You speak of duty, but not yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: In my eyes, Mavuika, you are not inherently special — a child of Natlan among countless others.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Yes, the situation is urgent and the Ley Lines must be restored right away, but it is too heavy a burden for you to shoulder alone.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That is where we differ, Lord of the Night. You see all humans as the same, but I understand what it means to be a leader.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: A leader is swift and decisive in the face of reality.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Someone capable of making the "right choice" even when there are no good options on the table.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Sacrificing the remainder of my life to help Natlan overcome this crisis... That is the right choice.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: After all, leadership is built on the trust of ordinary people. Without them, there is no Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The people look to their leader to make the world a better place and stand up for them when it counts.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: For that reason, I must see my duty through to the very end.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, what about you, Mavuika? You still haven't talked about what you want...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Is it that unimportant to you?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It's not important, Citlali.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: There is nothing more important than protecting the future we built together!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's hard to argue with her logic. She probably knew we would come and prepared what to say in advance.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It's time for Natlan to enter a new era, and I know she wants to fulfill her duty as a "leader," but...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She deserves to have a place in the future she built with her people.)

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: I shall accept Mavuika's sacrifice for the Lord of the Night as her death, and I will bear witness to the very end.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: Thus concludes the deal I made with Xbalanque several thousand years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: Lord of the Night, you may now begin.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: What are you waiting for?

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: There is another who wishes to take part in the ceremony, and I cannot disregard their intentions. I must wait for them to arrive.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Another...?

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: *sigh* I was to bear witness to a death, and now the situation is increasingly tenuous.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: If the life of this second individual fails to meet my requirements, I fear I may lose my patience.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Rest assured, his life will hold equal value. I am the helper of humanity, and I must always place their demands first, no matter who the human may be.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: Hm, cumbersome, but there is nothing to be done — such is the duty of an angel.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Wait, this feeling...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: *panting*... We made it.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Thank you for showing me the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Captain!?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The other individual you mentioned... It was him?

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Indeed. Like you, he carries many lofty ideals.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Mavuika, I understand how you feel, and if I were an ordinary mortal, I would have no reason to stop you.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: But, like you, I have been waiting for this day for too long, and I can offer a better solution.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: You created this new future, and you deserve to guide its direction. Your life should not end here.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: But, death... is the end I have been trying to reach all along. I have come this far to use my death to open the gates of the Ley Lines to my people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your people!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, the souls I saw in my dream?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: That's right. They have been with me for the past five hundred years.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: But, how!? Carrying that many souls within you... There's no way you could keep your consciousness intact!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Besides, you weren't affected by the Source Mechanism like I was.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Do you still remember the voice that you "heard"?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: It came from my heart. With the help of technology from Khaenri'ah, my heart was modified to convert memories and souls from the Ley Lines into knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: As a result, I became extremely sensitive to souls and developed the ability to sense their presence... much like yourself.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: After encountering countless lost souls during the disaster five hundred years ago, I forsook the capacity for knowledge granted by the modification and used my heart as a vessel instead.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: The lives of my comrades, as well as many Natlanese, have been stored here ever since.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: And you want to... send them home?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Yes. The Ley Lines will not accept them. But, by merging my existence with the Lord of the Night, I can become master of the Ley Lines and change the rules entirely.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: He expressed this to me, and I agreed.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: The Captain envisions a kinder and fairer set of rules for humanity. In addition, he aims to challenge the authority of the Ruler of Death... In a word, his goal is revenge.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: R—Revenge!?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: After all, it's because of her that I bear the curse of immortality, the curse of absolute life.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: I now understand that which you seek...

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Then, bear witness to my resolve and hatred.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: The people of Khaenri'ah committed grave sins, and for that we were cursed to suffer endless physical torment, cursed to witness the demise of everything we held dear.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: But, most of us were innocent. Most of us knew nothing of the Five Sinners' exploitation of Abyssal power... myself included.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: If I sacrifice my life for the Lord of the Night, you get the death you desire. But, at the same time, the curse of immortality would negate the very death you seek.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Left unresolved, that paradox could uproot the natural order of this world... Even you, great Ruler of Death, lack the capacity to bear the consequences of that outcome.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Your curse is now the tool with which I will overturn the oppression of the gods. This is my challenge to you...

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Forsake one of your rules — the choice is yours.

talks.objective: Witness the moment that the "rules" are upheld

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Captain, he...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: The curse of immortality still exists. Does that mean... The Captain will never move from this place?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Lord of the Night, is The Captain still with us?

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: There is no need to pursue traces of him. For those cursed with immortality, release from the mortal coil is the greatest form of peace.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Even so, please pass on my gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: His long journey has finally come to a close. I suppose... this is a happy ending for him.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I cannot imagine how much pain he endured over the past five hundred years... or how much strength it took to never stray from his goal.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: There's something I've been trying to figure out... I don't think I ever saw him sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I tried to ask him about it on the way here, but he didn't answer. Just like always, he never talks about himself...

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: It's probably due to the voices.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: When souls merge in a single being, their voices echo endlessly through the mind.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: Souls that retain memories of their death often scream and wail in despair... Considering the number of souls inside him, that effect would be even greater.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, over the past five hundred years, he didn't sleep... at all?

choices.text: No wonder Dain's method of slowing the decay of his body...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Without experiencing the curse of immortality, we will never truly know his agony.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: But, I can see why his hatred for the Ruler of Death was so strong.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: In the end, he used that immortality to his advantage and granted the Lord of the Night eternal life by fusing his existence with hers.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Well fought, Captain.

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: You may wonder why the Night Kingdom, a land of souls, was unable to accept the souls adrift on the surface...

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: The reason lies in the Heavenly Principles' modifications to the Ley Lines. The original purpose was to help counter the Abyss. And so, their stability was paramount.

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: But, at one point in time, Natlan's Ley Lines were decimated. Even after reconstruction, the rules needed for the Ode of Resurrection made it impossible to reconnect the Ley Lines to other nations.

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: That unique quality is precisely what drew The Captain to Natlan.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Did he try the same thing in other nations?

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: Yes, but all those attempts ended in failure.

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: He fought to save Natlan not only to defeat the Abyss, but because this is the only land where the souls within him could find salvation.

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: We met not long ago to talk about that very possibility, and I confirmed the feasibility of his plan.

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: I, too, recognized the need to change the rules of the Ley Lines, not only for the souls that wander this land, but for the outlanders that may perish here in the future...

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: In the eyes of the Heavenly Principles, that kind of change is extremely risky, if not impermissible... But, as an Angel, I have a duty to serve humanity — such is my mandate.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Thank you for everything.

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: Citlali, when I gave you the Pilgrim's Chronicle, I said something rather pessimistic to you... Do you remember?

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: How many years of life are enough? Ten? One hundred? I thought it made no difference...

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: But, now, I have the chance to live forever. I am immensely grateful to humanity for this gift, and I am deeply sorry I thought so little of it in the past.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You don't need to thank us. You bear a heavy responsibility.

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: Heavy? No. That responsibility is the purpose of my existence.

response.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
response.text: Farewell, humans, creators of miracles. A new era awaits you.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Looks like she returned to the Night Kingdom.

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: So, this was The Captain's goal all along...

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: He fought to the end for all those souls and challenged the rules of the world in the process.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: He was an outstanding warrior.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: He took on a burden that was meant for me and even brought about a better outcome... It would seem I lost this duel.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: He was right — Natlan needs a leader to guide its future. If not a successor, then that responsibility will continue to be mine to bear.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: But, for now, let us pay our final respects to this fallen hero.

choices.text: Didn't work for him.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: To my sister, Hine.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I know all that remains in the Night Kingdom is your memory, but I still wanted to write a short letter to tell you about the situation after the war.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: After countless partings and farewells, Natlan has finally entered an era of peace.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The Pilgrimage is still a popular tournament, but now, its only purpose is to showcase the thrill of competition rather than select warriors for war.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Our cultural legacy is not rooted in our suffering. In this era of peace, Natlan's fire will burn brighter than ever.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: With the restoration of the Night Kingdom, our people are now free to leave our borders, and many have set their sights on the wonders of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'm sure many exciting and eye-opening adventures await them.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: And although our battle scars will fade, the stories of our heroes will never be forgotten.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: When a new you returns to this land one day, I know you'll recognize the significance of this war and all we lost.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The land we love has not been destroyed, but grows stronger by the day.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I will forever be grateful that I got to see you again.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: And when the flames deliver this letter to you, I hope you know how much I miss you.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Huh, I actually got the chance to finish this painting.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: And not a moment too soon. It's time to bid farewell to all the fallen.

dialogues.speaker: Balam
dialogues.text: Don't worry, someone will show you the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's on your mind, Xilonen?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I was just thinking about your ancient name, "Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini." It's truly a perfect fit.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Seeing how much hope you've given to the people here... It makes that even more true.

talks.objective: Go to where the memorial ceremony is being held

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We are gathered here today to bid farewell to all who lost their lives in this war.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: This struggle has caused us profound pain and brought us face to face with loneliness and loss.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But, through it all, our bravery and resolve never wavered, and we never lost sight of victory.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Even the tiniest of sparks can unite to become a blazing fire.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: They lit our way forward and showed us the path to victory.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: When our homeland is revived, and life blooms again, they will return to us with the first rain of spring.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It is just as our poem describes:

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "We are the inheritors of memory and legend."

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "Those who grew alongside sun and wind."

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "Those who forged our own destiny and future."

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "That is Natlan's fire, the lifeblood of our nation."

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The fallen are never truly lost to us. We will be reunited one day.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: And as we create new legends and write new poems in honor of our beloved homeland, they will always be with us.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Their deeds immortalized in our memory, and their names immortalized in stone.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: This epic will be remembered in the actions of every valiant warrior and brave saurian, all equally important and indispensable.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I would also like to take the time to recognize a Fatui Harbinger who sacrificed his life for our cause.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: He was a warrior from Khaenri'ah who helped defend our nation five hundred years ago, a man who used his own heart as refuge for the souls of the fallen. For the chance to offer them a final resting place, he chose to fight with us once again.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: In the end, he fulfilled his wish and returned the souls to the Ley Lines. By turning his curse into a weapon, he defeated his fated foe and protected me in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We have had our differences in the past, and I cannot say his character is representative of all in his organization...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But, on this occasion, we honor him as one of our own. In Natlan, all heroes are worthy of celebration.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What are you thinking about, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, the battle, right? Even though we won in the end, it cost a lot to get to this point, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Monument
dialogues.text: "Sing your final song with pride, like a hero's march to the other side."

dialogues.speaker: Monument
dialogues.text: #"This monument commemorates the {ABYSSWAR#1003} brave warriors who gave their lives in the War for Natlan."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's leave this for them.

dialogues.speaker: Yata
dialogues.text: Story! Story! I wanna hear a story!

dialogues.speaker: Cucuya
dialogues.text: C'mon! Tell us! Tell us!

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: Well, you kids don't miss a beat, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: Alright, you can be the first audience for this new tale. Let me know what you think.

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: Now, where to begin...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wanna stop and listen to the story? Sounds pretty fun!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: This is a story of the great heroes of our time.

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: There are three great heroes at the center of this tale.

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: #The first is an outlander known as "{NICKNAME}."

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: A warrior of great strength, completely immune to the power of the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Sadigua
dialogues.text: #Most importantly, {NICKNAME} is kind and brave, someone who treasures those around h{M#im}{F#er}. You could call h{M#im}{F#er} a natural-born hero!

dialogues.speaker: Soncco
dialogues.text: #Yeah, {F#s}he's super strong! Tell us more!

dialogues.speaker: Ayun
dialogues.text: Hey, just let him finish the story!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #The man telling the story keeps looking this way, {NICKNAME}. Paimon thinks he recognizes you...

choices.text: Well, we've really made a name ourselves in Natlan.

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: The second hero is also an outlander.

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: Many years ago, he forged a connection with this land and used his body as a vessel for the souls of his fallen comrades.

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: His goal was to give them a home and, with that, a chance to be reborn into this world.

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: The third hero is none other than our current Archon, Mavuika!

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: Not only is she a powerful and respected figure, but she also commands the power of the Ode of Resurrection, which can bring people back from the dead.

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: With the support of six heroes from five hundred years ago, she united Natlan against a dangerous foe.

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: #Now, this story truly begins with the arrival of {NICKNAME} in Natlan...

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: #...Under h{M#is}{F#er} guidance, Kachina performed exceptionally well in the Pilgrimage, and earned her chance at the Night Warden Wars...

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: ...Suddenly, the sky turned dark, the Sacred Flame went out, and Gosoythoth appeared...

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: ...Everyone gathered at the Stadium and sang the Ode of Resurrection together to send their support to the furthest corner of the Night Kingdom...

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: "Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini" became known by all, and everyone began reciting the words that defined its message.

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: "In the beginning, there was darkness."

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: "Until someone set themselves aflame."

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: "Only then did the universe know light."

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: Anyway, the dust has now settled, and Natlan has entered a new era of peace.

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: #{NICKNAME} fought for "life." The Captain fought for "death."

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: And our Archon, Mavuika, created a bridge between them.

response.speaker: Yata
response.text: Wow!

response.speaker: Cucuya
response.text: Is there more? Please don't let that be the end!

response.speaker: Sadigua
response.text: Sounds like you like this one... Tell you what, give me some time, and I'll write it all out in even greater detail.

response.speaker: Matho
response.text: I loved it! This is the best story ever!

response.speaker: Soncco
response.text: Yeah! And "Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini" is the coolest ancient name! I get to be "Tumaini" today, okay guys?

response.speaker: Ayun
response.text: Hey, it's supposed to be my turn!

response.speaker: Cucuya
response.text: No! It's my turn!

response.speaker: Yata
response.text: No, it's MY turn! I get to be "Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini" today!

response.speaker: Matho
response.text: So, no one wants to be the Pyro Archon anymore?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hehe, sounds fun. What do you say, {NICKNAME}? Wanna let Paimon be "Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini" for the day?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure! Then, I'll be Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alrighty then! Let's go, Paimon. A new adventure awaits!

choices.text: Listening to all this is a little embarrassing, though...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, do you think Xbalanque could have met the Ruler of Death in Cinder City, the one they call... Ochkanatlan?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's very likely. After all, Ochkanatlan was built on the site of a previous Dragon city — it's known as the first city of the Pyro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Then, let's head over right away!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's not easy to get there, so follow me — I'll take you.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Go on. Everyone's waiting for your victory parade.

dialogues.speaker: Wakanka
dialogues.text: Thank you for indulging everyone. It meant a lot to them.

dialogues.speaker: Wuttunee
dialogues.text: Thanks again for the autographs.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Why does no one ask for the autograph of the Almighty Dragonlord K'uhul Ajaw!?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Ajaw was just practicing his signature with a rock. Still waiting on the admirers, though...

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: HEY! Keep it to yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Olapa
dialogues.text: Huh? It's the great hero! Please, come dance with us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Whoa! Wh—What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Should we join them?

choices.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>Let's give it a whirl.</color>

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright! Paimon's always willing to try something new!

response.speaker: Olapa
response.text: Hey, not bad! You're a natural!

response.speaker: Alakai
response.text: Let's hear it for our hero!

choices.text: I—I think I'll pass.

response.speaker: Alakai
response.text: That's alright! Let's hear it for our hero!

dialogues.speaker: Olapa
dialogues.text: For music, and for the Sacred Flame!

dialogues.speaker: Alakai
dialogues.text: Ohh!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: When Guthred's soul possessed my body, all I saw was a dark abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: The Captain carried countless souls within him. It must have taken so much strength to live like that for hundreds of years...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: For us, his death is something sad. But for him... maybe it finally allowed him to be at peace.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hey, did you hear? As long as we get permission from our chief, we can leave Natlan as much as we want!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's because the Ley Lines have been restored, right? And the Lord of the Night is a lot stronger now!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That means we can finally see the outside world for ourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I heard that Fontaine has a HUGE ocean! That is totally my vibe! I can't wait to go see it!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I wanna go to Liyue! The mountains are supposed to be super tall!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Sounds like the makings of a great vacation! Let's start planning!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: But, first, we all promised we would go to the hot springs together! Hehe, then we'll be "hot spring buddies" for life!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: My teacher once said, "the weight of fate is decided by the one who has to bear it."

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You helped Natlan overcome a cruel fate. From now on, we will always be there to help you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Now, we just need to see where your fate... no, "our fate" leads us.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Strange... Why does no one praise the deeds of the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Does no one care about my heroism? A great hero such as myself, forced to remain nameless. Hmph, ignorant fools...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Fine, I guess you helped out. Good job.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Well, well, well... A compliment! After all these years! It's about time you knew your place, lowly servant.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Hey! Why are you glaring at me? Oof—

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The stories of heroes will continue to be passed down from generation to generation.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: If Natlan faces a crisis again, I'm sure people will look to our story as a source of hope.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: We've earned our place in history... That's pretty surreal, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Muscles grow stronger through periods of strain, and people work the same way.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Even though the crisis is over, we will still band together for the sake of a new future!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Oh, and you should really come to the Collective of Plenty sometime. Especially you, Paimon — your nutrition plan is already set!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... Um, so you can help Paimon get stronger, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #If something like this happens again, Paimon wants to fight by {NICKNAME}'s side!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Haha, of course! You've got serious potential!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: After you got back, you mentioned that you saw Chuychu in the Night Kingdom... So, she helped you, then?

choices.text: Yeah, she brought a lot of Saurians.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Good. I'm sure that made her happy.

choices.text: There's still time.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: It's alright. I don't think she's going to come see me.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: She's probably sick of nagging her older sister.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Still, thank you for telling me. Natlan has a bright future because of you, and I have a chance to make up for my regrets.

choices.text: To see her in your dreams.
And helped get through a tricky part of the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Chimalli
dialogues.text: Just like the Archon said — we can now proudly tell our children that this war is a thing of the past. It's a new chapter for all of us.

dialogues.speaker: Chimalli
dialogues.text: We will never forget your contribution, and Natlan will always be with you. May the Sacred Flame protect you in all the journeys to come.

dialogues.speaker: Luta
dialogues.text: When I was little, my father told me about Thrain, the "Sentinel Knight," an outlander who once fought alongside the warriors of Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Luta
dialogues.text: He was brave, fearless, and deeply respected by his men. I always wished I could go back in time and see him in action...

dialogues.speaker: Luta
dialogues.text: I never thought that, in my lifetime, another outlander would fight to save this land, or that I would get the chance to fight by their side. I will treasure this honor for the rest of my life.

dialogues.speaker: Huamanga
dialogues.text: I knew about The Captain's immense strength, but I never expected him to have a such a strong sense of honor.

dialogues.speaker: Huamanga
dialogues.text: No matter how prejudiced I may have been in the past, he now has my utmost respect.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Ah, our hero is here! Is there something you want to discuss?

choices.text: About the stances of the Heavenly Principles and the Shades...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The forces of the Abyss have always sought to corrode Teyvat. The Ley Lines were created by the Heavenly Principles, and it is only with their protection that Teyvat is able to nurture all forms of life.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: If the Abyss had free reign, this world would become a living hell. We saw that for ourselves...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Any attempt by humanity to harness the power of the Abyss is met with swift punishment. The Heavenly Principles and the Shades show no mercy in that regard.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: That unyielding approach is also the source of great sorrow and hatred... The situation goes beyond a simple discussion of "right" versus "wrong."

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Perhaps the truth will reveal itself during your future adventures.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The long journey of the Pyro Archon has now come to an end. Together, we overcame darkness and death to accomplish something truly remarkable.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: As we celebrate your glory, allow me thank you once again — this time, just as "Mavuika."

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Thank you for the respect, understanding, and support every step of the way.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It was my honor.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: An honor we share.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: You can keep chatting with your friends nearby. I think I'll stay here for now... and watch over them.

choices.text: About the Ode of Resurrection somehow taking effect before victory...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Oh, isn't it obvious?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The Ode of Resurrection didn't take effect at all.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Your own strength is what allowed you to keep fighting, as well as the moral support from everyone in Natlan.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Still, "moral support" is also an important, if under appreciated, effect of the Ode of Resurrection.

choices.text: About Natlan's Gnosis...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The Captain's subordinates sent us a letter he left behind. After our duel at the Stadium, he asked the Tsaritsa to remove him from the responsibility of obtaining the Gnosis, and his request was granted.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The Captain respected the outcome of that match and refused to violate his principles. But, since this is the final Gnosis, I doubt the Tsaritsa will let the situation stand.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Perhaps a replacement Harbinger will be sent here soon. I'll make sure to be prepared.

choices.text: About the next stop on my journey...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: A direct conflict with the Fatui is unavoidable the moment you step foot in Snezhnaya.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: So, make sure you're ready for any scenario. On a related note, I've acquired some new intel about the fragment that suddenly appeared in the sky.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Such fragments are known as "Ancient Moon's Remnants," relics of Secret Source technology from the era of the Ancient Dragons. Coincidentally, a small squad of Fatui infiltrated our borders around the same time it appeared.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Our investigation revealed them to be subordinates of The Doctor. Their stronghold is in Nod-Krai, a land with a long history not far from Snezhnaya.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The people there can use a very special power. It is said that this mysterious power predates even the seven elements of Teyvat.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Ancient Moon's Remnants, The Doctor, a mysterious power... The project that connects all three must be ambitious indeed.

choices.text: About the tribe my ancient name will belong to...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Tribe? Oh, you're thinking along the lines of how the names of the six heroes were inherited...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: In truth, apart from a few ancient names associated with a certain tribal culture or tradition, most ancient names can be inherited by anyone.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Your name likely falls under that category. The Wayob will select someone who shares your character and name them as your successor.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Of course, that won't happen for a very long time.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't have any other questions...

dialogues.speaker: Rotchev
dialogues.text: My lord, you will forever serve as an example for all your soldiers.

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: Roar!

dialogues.speaker: Toch
dialogues.text: Roar—

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: #Hey, stop running around! You're blocking h{M#is}{F#er} way!

dialogues.speaker: Khadija
dialogues.text: Great hero! Could you look this way for a sec?

dialogues.speaker: Wichasa
dialogues.text: Can I take a picture of you? Please!

dialogues.speaker: Hinekea
dialogues.text: As the sun shines down on our nation...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Another victory for Natlan!

dialogues.speaker: Yata
dialogues.text: Over here! Over here!

dialogues.speaker: Yata
dialogues.text: There's a bunch of people waiting for you here, too!

dialogues.speaker: Cuallee
dialogues.text: Thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Ayamis
dialogues.text: I'll treasure this for the rest of my life!

dialogues.speaker: Lautaro
dialogues.text: The hero's autograph... I actually got the hero's autograph!

dialogues.speaker: Kyssa
dialogues.text: Great hero, we prepared some snacks and drinks for you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon can take those!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #These Saurus Crackers are the best! You should try some, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Pezuta
dialogues.text: It's the great hero! Quick, get ready to take a picture!

dialogues.speaker: Kinyan
dialogues.text: Over here! Over here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, they're dancing!

dialogues.speaker: Olapa
dialogues.text: For music, for the Sacred Flame, and for our heroes!

dialogues.speaker: Alakai
dialogues.text: Ooh!

dialogues.speaker: Quidel
dialogues.text: Quick, take a picture! We can turn it into graffiti!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: #Look over here, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Hiia
dialogues.text: Woohoo!

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: The great hero is here!

dialogues.speaker: #{REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}
dialogues.text: Roar, roar ♪

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you're here too! And you brought a bunch of friends!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Man, this place really is hard to get to... And, um, Paimon wasn't the only one who saw that weird... thing up there, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All those... eyes inside of it... Talk about creepy!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I believe that's how the Ruler of Death keeps an eye on Teyvat...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Quick, this way. We're almost there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, it's Mavuika!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, is that part new? Paimon's never seen it before!
